title: The Bakery on Our Street
intro: Mr Joseph bakes fresh bread every morning. Adjectives are describing words that tell us more about a thing.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: An adjective is a describing word.
In 'a round bun', the adjective is 'bun'.
'Golden' tells us how the bread looks.

sections.title: Write the adjective in each group of words.
Match each adjective to the thing it describes best.
Add the adjective in brackets to the sentence.

items.a: The baker held a heavy tray.

sections.title: Write two sentences about your favourite bakery treat. Use an adjective in each.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I love soft doughnuts. Check for one adjective in each sentence.

title: A Rainy Evening on the Balcony
intro: Ishaan is watching the rain with his grandfather. Some adjectives tell us how things look and some tell us how they sound.

sections.title: Sort the words. Do they tell how something looks or sounds?
Fill in with a word from the box: booming, squeaky, gentle, buzzing.

items.q: The old gate made a ___ noise.
A ___ mosquito flew near my ear.

sections.title: Circle the adjective that fits.
Add the adjective in brackets to the sentence.

items.q: The dog barked at the rain. (noisy)
items.a: The noisy dog barked at the rain.

sections.title: Write two sentences about the sounds of a rainy day.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I heard loud thunder. Check for a sound adjective in each sentence.

title: The Spice Souk
intro: Layla and her aunt are walking past sacks of spices. Use adjectives to tell how things smell and look.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: 'Spicy' can tell us how something smells.
'Stinky' is a word for a nice smell.

sections.title: Sort the smell words.
Fill in with a word from the box: red, long, yellow.

items.q: The ___ chillies looked like little flames.

sections.title: Match each smell word to the thing.
Add the adjective in brackets to the sentence.

items.a: The shopkeeper opened a dusty sack.

title: Lunch Box Swap
intro: Class 2 is sharing lunch today. Use adjectives to tell how food tastes and feels.

sections.title: Sort the words. Do they tell how something tastes or feels?
Match each taste to the food.
Circle the adjective that fits.
Write the sentence again. Put a comma between the two adjectives.

items.q: I ate a sweet sticky ladoo.
items.a: I ate a sweet, sticky ladoo.

items.q: Bela had a hot spicy samosa.
items.a: Bela had a hot, spicy samosa.

sections.title: Write two sentences about your lunch. Tell how it tastes.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. My dosa was crisp and salty. Check for taste adjectives.

title: The Pet Shop Visit
intro: Noah and his sister are choosing a pet. When two adjectives come together, put a comma between them.

sections.title: Sort the words. Do they tell how something feels or sounds?
Write the two adjectives.
Circle the adjective that fits.
Add the two adjectives in brackets. Use a comma.

items.q: The puppy licked my hand. (small, brown)
items.a: The small, brown puppy licked my hand.

items.q: A hamster ran in its wheel. (fat, sleepy)
items.a: A fat, sleepy hamster ran in its wheel.

sections.title: Describe a pet you like. Use two adjectives with a comma.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I like the soft, white rabbit. Check the comma between the adjectives.

title: A Night at the Desert Camp
intro: Rashid's family is spending the night in the dunes. Use all five senses to describe it.

sections.title: Match each sentence to the body part.
Sort each word under the right sense.
Fill in with a word from the box: cool, sweet, bright, loud.

items.q: The sand felt ___ under my feet at night.

sections.title: Add the two adjectives in brackets. Use a comma.

items.q: The camel sat on the sand. (tall, sleepy)
items.a: The tall, sleepy camel sat on the sand.

items.q: We sat near the fire. (warm, crackling)
items.a: We sat near the warm, crackling fire.

sections.title: Write two sentences about the desert at night. Use two senses.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I saw the round, white moon. I heard soft music. Check for sense adjectives.

title: Grandma's Garden in Pune
intro: Mihika is helping Aaji in her garden. Which sense does each describing word use?

sections.title: Which sense? Write see, hear, smell, taste or feel.
Circle the adjective that fits.
Write the missing comma or full stop.

items.q: The garden has tall ___ shady trees.
A fat ___ green caterpillar ate a leaf.
Aaji waters the plants every morning ___
I picked a small ___ red tomato.

sections.title: Use the two adjectives to describe the first naming word. Use a comma.

items.q: The squirrel ran up the tree. (quick, grey)
items.a: The quick, grey squirrel ran up the tree.

items.q: Mud stuck to my shoes. (wet, sticky)
items.a: Wet, sticky mud stuck to my shoes.

sections.title: Write two sentences about a garden. Tell what you see and smell.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I see bright, orange flowers. Check for adjectives and the comma.

title: The School Fun Fair
intro: The playground is full of stalls and games today. Describe the fun with good adjectives.

sections.title: Match each adjective to the thing it describes best.
Circle True or False.

items.q: 'a big, red balloon' is written correctly.
'a tall thin, clown' is written correctly.
'The fair was noisy.' has two adjectives.
'I won a soft, cuddly panda.' has two adjectives.

sections.title: Fill in with a word from the box: spinning, sweet, noisy, slippery.

items.q: The ___ wheel went round and round.
The ___ crowd cheered for the clown.

sections.title: Write the sentence again. Put in the missing comma.

items.q: We rode a fast scary roller coaster.
items.a: We rode a fast, scary roller coaster.

items.q: Tomas wore a tall shiny hat.
items.a: Tomas wore a tall, shiny hat.

sections.title: Write two sentences about a stall you would like to run.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I would sell cold, fizzy drinks. Check for adjectives.

title: Making Lemonade
intro: It is a hot afternoon and Daniyal is making lemonade with his mother. Describe each step.

sections.title: Sort the describing words.
Circle the adjective that fits.
Write the adjective from each sentence.

items.q: Mama cut a big lemon. The adjective is ___.
The tangy juice made me blink. The adjective is ___.
We used a wooden spoon. The adjective is ___.
The jug was heavy. The adjective is ___.

sections.title: Add the two adjectives in brackets. Use a comma.

items.a: I drank the cool, sweet lemonade.

items.q: Pips fell into the bowl. (small, slippery)
items.a: Small, slippery pips fell into the bowl.

sections.title: Write how to make your favourite drink. Use three adjectives.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. Pour cold milk into a tall glass. Add sweet syrup. Check for three adjectives.

title: A Boat Ride on Dubai Creek
intro: Sana and her cousins are crossing the creek on an abra. What can they see, hear, smell and feel?

sections.title: Which sense? Write see, hear, smell, taste or feel.
Circle True or False.

items.q: 'The old, wooden boat rocked.' uses two adjectives.
A comma goes after the second adjective.
'Sparkling' tells us how the water tastes.

sections.title: Fill in with a word from the box: screeching, cool, tall, crowded.

items.q: A ___ breeze blew on my face.
We saw ___ towers across the water.
The ___ boat had no empty seats.

sections.title: Make each sentence longer with the two adjectives. Use a comma.

items.q: We sat on a bench. (long, narrow)
items.a: We sat on a long, narrow bench.

sections.title: Describe the creek. Tell what you see and hear.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I see small, brown boats. I hear noisy birds. Check for adjectives.

title: The Vegetable Market in Kochi
intro: Appu is shopping with his grandmother on a busy morning. Make every sentence paint a picture.

sections.title: Sort each word under the right sense.
Circle the adjective that fits.
Add both adjectives. Each one describes a different naming word.

items.a: The cheerful woman sold ripe bananas.

items.q: A boy carried a basket. (thin, heavy)
items.a: A thin boy carried a heavy basket.

sections.title: Match the two adjectives to the vegetable.
Make this sentence longer and better: The man sold fish.
sections.a: e.g. The loud, smiling man sold fresh, silver fish. Check for at least two adjectives and the commas.

title: Lohri Bonfire Night
intro: Gurleen's family is celebrating Lohri in Amritsar. Describe the fire, the food and the music.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: In 'the warm, orange fire', the comma is in the right place.

sections.title: Fill in with a word from the box: roasted, thumping, freezing, glowing, sweet.

items.q: Dadi gave us hot, ___ peanuts in their shells.
I chewed a ___ piece of jaggery.
The ___ sparks rose into the sky.

sections.title: Write the two adjectives.
Add both adjectives. Each one describes a different naming word.

items.q: Smoke rose into the sky. (grey, starry)
items.a: Grey smoke rose into the starry sky.

sections.title: Make this sentence longer and better: The fire burned.
sections.a: e.g. The huge, golden fire burned in the cold field. Check for at least two adjectives.

title: A Day at the Aquarium
intro: Class 2 is walking through the glass tunnel. Describe the sea animals so a friend can picture them.

sections.title: Match the two adjectives to the sea animal.
Circle the adjective that fits.

items.before: A ray swam past like a

sections.title: Finish with looks, sounds, smells, tastes or feels.
Join the sentences into one. Use both adjectives with a comma.

items.q: I saw a crab. It was red. It was spiky.
items.a: I saw a red, spiky crab.

items.q: A diver fed the fish. They were big. They were hungry.
items.a: A diver fed the big, hungry fish.

sections.title: Describe a sea animal. Do not say its name.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. It is a small, orange fish with white stripes. Check for adjectives.

title: Camping in the Hatta Mountains
intro: Oliver's family has pitched a tent near the rocks. Use your senses to describe the night.

sections.title: Sort the describing words.
Write the naming word that is described.
Fill in with a word from the box: burnt, bubbling, starlit, heavy.

items.q: I carried a ___ backpack up the hill.

sections.title: Join the sentences into one. Use both adjectives with a comma.

items.q: We found a cave. It was dark. It was damp.
items.a: We found a dark, damp cave.

items.q: Papa lit a lamp. It was small. It was bright.
items.a: Papa lit a small, bright lamp.

sections.title: Write three sentences about a night outdoors. Use a different sense in each.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. I saw tiny stars. I heard a hooting owl. The ground felt hard. Check each sentence uses a different sense.

title: The Old Lighthouse Story
intro: Farida is writing a spooky story for the class book. Help her choose adjectives that set the scene.

sections.title: Circle the better adjective for a spooky story.
Finish with see, hear, smell or feel.

items.q: 'The air was stale and fishy.' You ___ this.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: 'The tall, white lighthouse stood on a rock.' has the comma in the right place.
'A loud, bang shook the door.' is written correctly.
Adjectives help the reader picture the story.

sections.title: Add both pairs of adjectives. Use commas.

items.q: The keeper carried a lantern. (old, kind) (heavy, brass)
items.a: The old, kind keeper carried a heavy, brass lantern.

items.q: A gull sat on the wall. (fat, white) (low, stone)
items.a: A fat, white gull sat on the low, stone wall.

sections.title: Write the start of your own story. Use at least four adjectives.
sections.a: Answers will vary. Check for at least four adjectives and a comma between two adjectives in a row.
